articles.title: Princess Catherine's cancer journey to be depicted in new show
articles.summary: Catherine has spoken about how "cancer does change you" in a documentary that will be screened on BBC One on 29 November.
articles.body:
The Princess of Wales' cancer journey is set to be depicted in a new BBC documentary "Heal" that will air next weekend.

It follows Catherine announcing in January 2025 that she was in remission after having revealed her diagnosis less than a year prior.

She has since spoken openly about her illness and treatment although has never disclosed publicly what type of cancer she faced.

The new documentary will include footage of her completing the Three Peaks Challenge earlier this year.

"It changes your body, it changes you physically - but there is a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you," she says.

articles.title: 'Grow a spine': Youth Congress workers storm Meta office premises in Hyderabad; issue ultimatum
articles.summary: HYDERABAD: Telangana Youth Congress leaders staged a protest and allegedly vandalised property at Meta’s office in Raidurgam on Friday, accusing the
articles.body: HYDERABAD: Telangana Youth Congress leaders staged a protest and allegedly vandalised property at Meta’s office in Raidurgam on Friday, accusing the company of blocking the social media accounts of national-level Youth Congress leaders Uday Bhanu and Manish Sharma.Police said around 25 Congress activists carrying placards entered the access-controlled Sky View premises, which houses Meta’s office, around 3pm.The protesters raised slogans, ran through the property and damaged flower pots and other objects in a corridor before staging a sit-in.The protesters accused Meta of working under BJP’s influence and demanded restoration of the blocked accounts.Raidurgam police reached the premises and attempted to control the protesters, who allegedly created panic and tried to evade them. Police initially said 20 protesters were taken into custody.Raidurgam inspector T Bhupathi later said Telangana Youth Congress state president Jakkidi Shiva Charan Reddy and 20 others were taken into preventive custody when they arrived to protest against Meta’s office.All were released on bail after providing the necessary sureties.'Grow a spine'Later in the day the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) escalated its confrontation with social media giant, issuing a sharp seven-day ultimatum accusing the platform of political censorship and acting at the behest of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).In a post on X addressing "BJP ka Beta - META," the Youth Congress declared that India is a democracy rather than "Modi's private property," and warned the company to restore restricted accounts and posts within seven days.Calling on Meta to "grow a spine" and operate as a neutral platform rather than a "BJP's frontal organisation," and threatened escalations "in the courts, on the streets, and at your offices too" if its demands are not met.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news. articles.title: Sem água há 4 dias, moradora usa chuva para manter rotina | G1
articles.standfirst: Família de Bom Jesus do Itabapoana contou com ajuda de vizinhos para tomar banho durante período sem abastecimento.
articles.summary: Família de Bom Jesus do Itabapoana contou com ajuda de vizinhos para tomar banho durante período sem abastecimento.
articles.body:
Moradores do Bairro Novo, em Bom Jesus do Itabapoana , no Noroeste Fluminense, relataram que ficaram quatro dias sem abastecimento de água.

Durante a interrupção, uma das moradoras recorreu à água da chuva armazenada em uma caixa extra para dar descarga no banheiro. Para tomar banho, a família contou com a ajuda de vizinhos.

Em um vídeo gravado em casa, a moradora mostra as torneiras sem água, o tanque vazio e a caixa onde armazena a água da chuva. Segundo ela, a reserva ajudou a família a manter parte da rotina durante o período sem abastecimento.

Falta de água faz moradora depender de reserva de chuva por quatro dias em Bom Jesus do Itabapoana — Foto: Blog Alan Gonçalves

Em nota, a Cedae informou que o motor de uma bomba que atende a região apresentou um problema mecânico na noite de quarta-feira (18).

O reparo foi concluído na manhã de quinta-feira (19). Ainda na quinta-feira, segundo a companhia, uma falha no fornecimento de energia elétrica pela Enel também afetou o abastecimento.

De acordo com a Cedae, o fornecimento de energia foi restabelecido na manhã de sexta-feira (20) e, desde então, o abastecimento de água foi normalizado.

A companhia orienta os moradores que ainda estiverem sem água a ligar para o número 0800 282 1195 para solicitar o envio de um caminhão-pipa.

articles.title: Chuvas deixam 40% de cidade alagada em MS, diz prefeito | G1
articles.standfirst: Porto Murtinho voltou a ser atingida por uma chuva intensa na madrugada deste sábado (21). Casas ficaram cercadas pela água, ruas estão intransitáveis e prefeitura avalia decretar situação de emergência.
articles.summary: A chuva em Porto Murtinho acumulou 230 mm neste sábado, triplicando a média mensal e deixando famílias ilhadas em meio a ruas intransitáveis e casas alagadas em MS.
articles.body:
Ruas inteiras debaixo d'água, casas ilhadas e moradores com dificuldade para sair de suas residências. Esse é o cenário em Porto Murtinho (MS), após uma sequência de chuvas intensas que voltou a atingir o município na madrugada deste sábado (21). Segundo o prefeito Nelson Cintra (PSDB), cerca de 40% da cidade ficou alagada e cerca de 50 famílias foram desabrigadas. Imagens feitas por drone nesta manhã mostram a dimensão da inundação nos bairros Cohab e Dom Pepe. Veja o vídeo acima.

A nova chuva atingiu a cidade justamente quando a água dos temporais anteriores começava a baixar. Segundo o prefeito, foram 230 milímetros entre a madrugada e o início da manhã deste sábado.

O g1 solicitou ao Centro de Monitoramento do Tempo e do Clima de Mato Grosso do Sul (Cemtec) os dados oficiais sobre o volume de chuva registrado no município, mas não teve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Cintra afirmou que foi a maior chuva que já presenciou na cidade.

"É um dilúvio, é um dilúvio, inundou quase metade da cidade", disse o prefeito.

Diante da situação, a prefeitura avalia decretar situação de emergência e pedir ajuda ao governo estadual. Segundo Cintra, as equipes municipais estão nas ruas para atender os moradores e contabilizar os prejuízos. Por isso, ainda não há um balanço atualizado de quantas pessoas ficaram desabrigadas ou desalojadas após a chuva deste sábado.

dea uma legenda p essa foto Imagem de drone mostra ruas submersas e casas cercadas pela água após sequência de chuvas intensas em Porto Murtinho, neste sábado (21). — Foto: Edoart Neumann

Ruas intransitáveis e casas cercadas pela água

As imagens registradas por um morador na manhã deste sábado mostram ruas completamente submersas e a água espalhada por extensas áreas residenciais. Em alguns trechos, a inundação tomou as vias e avançou pelos quintais, dificultando o acesso às casas.

O bairro Cohab, que já havia sido atingido na quinta-feira (19), voltou a registrar alagamentos. Na ocasião, a água invadiu residências nas ruas Carandá e Jatobá, e moradores precisaram retirar móveis e pertences.

A prefeitura divulgou novos alertas sobre pontos sem condições de passagem. A Rua 13 de Junho está alagada e intransitável. Na Avenida Laranjeiras, os dois lados da via estão tomados pela água. Já no Valetão, ao lado do Bogado, houve transbordamento.

A administração municipal também alertou para o risco de queda em bueiros abertos e orientou a população a evitar os trechos alagados.

Segundo o prefeito, a chuva parou durante a manhã e o nível da água começou a baixar. Ele explicou que os canais de drenagem não conseguiram escoar todo o volume recebido em poucas horas. A previsão divulgada pela prefeitura para este sábado indicava pancadas isoladas de chuva.

Casas e ruas completamente alagadas neste sábado (21) — Foto: Reprodução

Os alagamentos já haviam mobilizado equipes de resgate durante a semana. Na quinta-feira, o Corpo de Bombeiros utilizou viaturas para chegar às casas atingidas, enquanto tratores ficaram à disposição para ajudar os moradores a retirar móveis e outros pertences.

Com os estragos provocados pelas chuvas, a Secretaria Municipal de Assistência Social iniciou uma campanha de arrecadação para ajudar as famílias atingidas.

Estão sendo recebidos móveis, eletrodomésticos, roupas, lençóis e toalhas, todos em boas condições de uso. As doações podem ser entregues no Centro de Convivência do Idoso (CCI).

Mesmo antes da chuva deste sábado, Porto Murtinho já havia recebido quase três vezes o volume esperado para todo o mês de novembro.

Segundo o Cemtec, entre os dias 1º e 19, o município acumulou 429,6 milímetros de chuva, o equivalente a 2,6 vezes a média histórica de novembro, de 165 milímetros.

Somente entre quarta-feira (18) e quinta-feira (19), foram registrados 171 milímetros.

O meteorologista Vinicius Sperling explicou que a sequência de chuvas deixou o solo encharcado, dificultando a absorção de mais água e aumentando o risco de alagamentos.

Segundo ele, as chuvas intensas foram provocadas pela combinação de calor, alta umidade e um sistema de baixa pressão atmosférica localizado no norte do Paraguai, próximo à divisa com Mato Grosso do Sul.

articles.title: Nicarágua: governo Ortega impede entrada de cidadãos no país | G1
articles.standfirst: ONU documentou ao menos 318 casos de nicaraguenses impedidos de entrar no próprio país entre junho de 2018 e agosto de 2025.
articles.summary: O governo Ortega na Nicarágua impediu centenas de cidadãos de voltarem ao país, forçando nicaraguenses ao exílio ou a entradas clandestinas por trilhas perigosas.
articles.body:
A ONU documentou pelo menos 318 casos de nicaraguenses impedidos de entrar em seu próprio país entre junho de 2018 e agosto de 2025 — Foto: Ezequiel Becerra/AFP via Getty Images

"Comecei a andar porque sentia que não conseguia respirar direito, porque estava desesperado e porque também não tinha mais nada a fazer."

Minutos antes, Manuel havia chegado ao aeroporto de Barajas, em Madri, para pegar um voo de volta à Nicarágua, após uma viagem de férias.

No entanto, quando se aproximou do balcão da companhia aérea para despachar as malas, seus planos foram por água abaixo.

A funcionária que o atendeu disse: "Sinto muito, mas o governo do seu país não permite que você entre".

Em um pedaço de papel, ela anotou um endereço de e-mail do Ministério do Interior da Nicarágua para o qual ele poderia escrever. A BBC Mundo, serviço espanhol da BBC, teve acesso ao documento.

Manuel, nome fictício que usaremos por motivos de segurança, sentiu um frio percorrer o corpo. Viu sua pele se arrepiar, percebeu que o coração estava acelerado e sentiu um frio na barriga.

Por alguns segundos, ele teve a sensação de que o burburinho daquele aeroporto havia desaparecido.

Em um pedido inútil e sem sentido, respondeu à funcionária: "Não pode ser! Verifique novamente, por favor. Eu preciso ir embora, tenho que ir para o meu país. Não moro aqui, estou de férias. Onde vou ficar?"

Ele saiu da fila com as malas e começou a caminhar sem rumo.

"Fui para um canto e me sentei no chão para chorar. Lembro que ninguém se aproximou para me perguntar: 'Você está bem? O que aconteceu?'. É uma sensação horrível, de abandono. É algo que nunca senti na vida, nunca", conta.

Dias depois, prometeu a si mesmo que entraria na Nicarágua de qualquer jeito.

Manuel viveu em um 'limbo' antes de deixar a Nicarágua novamente — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

E foi isso que ele fez. Entrou clandestinamente, por trilhas, atravessando a faixa de fronteira que separa a Nicarágua de Honduras.

"Viver ilegalmente no próprio país — porque não há outra maneira de descrever isso — gera uma enorme ansiedade", afirma ele, agora de volta a Madri, onde está dando entrada em um pedido de asilo.

O caso dele não é isolado na Nicarágua. O Grupo de Especialistas em Direitos Humanos da ONU (GHREN, na sigla em inglês) documentou ao menos 318 casos de pessoas impedidas de entrar no país entre junho de 2018 e agosto de 2025.

A maioria permanece fora da Nicarágua, no exílio, solicitando asilo. Mas há também quem retorne por pontos da fronteira sem fiscalização e passe a viver em silêncio e com muitos cuidados.

A BBC Mundo entrou em contato por e-mail com a copresidente da Nicarágua, Rosario Murillo, para obter sua versão da história. Ela limitou-se a responder: "Agradeço seu interesse".

Em novembro de 2024, a Assembleia Nacional da Nicarágua, alinhada ao presidente Daniel Ortega e à esposa dele, Murillo, reformou a Lei de Migração e Estrangeiros para legalizar a negativa de entrada no país, as expulsões e a perda da nacionalidade.

A reforma concede à Direção-Geral de Migração e Estrangeiros poderes para "autorizar ou negar a entrada, revogar a permanência, cancelar a residência ou a nacionalidade nicaraguense adquirida".

Também inclui uma alteração ao Código Penal que prevê pena de dois a seis anos de prisão para os nicaraguenses que entrarem, saírem ou tentarem sair do território nacional de forma irregular com o objetivo de "prejudicar a integridade, a independência, a soberania e a autodeterminação da nação".

Em novembro de 2024, a Assembleia Nacional da Nicarágua reformou a Lei de Migração e Estrangeiros para legalizar a negativa de entrada no país — Foto: Oswaldo Rivas/AFP via Getty Images

Em novembro de 2025, a ministra do Interior, María Amelia Coronel, defendeu a política de negar, de forma discricionária, a entrada de nicaraguenses e estrangeiros no país.

Ela afirmou que o governo continuaria adotando essa medida contra todas as pessoas que considerasse representar um risco à "segurança nacional".

"Nós e todos os países somos soberanos, e a Nicarágua reserva-se o direito de admissão ao país em diversos casos relacionados à segurança nacional, à ordem pública e à prevenção de crimes", disse Coronel a um veículo de comunicação alinhado ao governo.

"Fazemos isso, sobretudo, porque temos amparo legal para fazê-lo e, acima de tudo, para proteger a soberania nacional e a segurança dos nossos cidadãos, que são o mais importante para o Ministério do Interior e para toda a Nicarágua."

Esse cenário se soma à decisão do governo, em 2023, de revogar a cidadania de 316 nicaraguenses considerados opositores — medida que o então secretário de Estado dos Estados Unidos, Antony Blinken, classificou como "mais um retrocesso para o povo nicaraguense e mais um passo na consolidação de um regime autocrático".

O governo de Daniel Ortega e Rosario Murillo revogou a cidadania de dezenas de nicaraguenses — Foto: Marvin Recinos/AFP via Getty Images

A mesma medida também foi aplicada, em setembro de 2024, a 135 presos expulsos para a Guatemala.

Soma-se a isso a reforma constitucional aprovada pela Assembleia Nacional em janeiro de 2025, que elimina o direito à dupla nacionalidade.

Críticos denunciam que, ao longo dos anos, o governo de Daniel Ortega e Rosario Murillo reprimiu a dissidência, recorrendo à violência contra manifestantes, enfraquecendo as instituições democráticas e realizando detenções em massa.

Manuel havia viajado à Espanha como turista. Estava sozinho e pretendia encontrar alguns amigos e familiares no país.

Ele admite que estava nervoso, mas não sentia nada diferente do que qualquer outro nicaraguense sente ao deixar o país atualmente, devido ao rigoroso controle migratório e à vigilância do governo.

"Todos nós que precisamos viajar para fora da Nicarágua em algum momento sentimos sempre aquele medinho. Por isso, na véspera da viagem, antes de chegar ao aeroporto de Manágua, entrei no meu Facebook e verifiquei se estava tudo limpo. Deletei minhas contas, uma coisa maluca, de alguém completamente perturbado. Bloqueei meu e-mail, apaguei tudo, para que não encontrassem alguma coisa, mesmo que não houvesse nada para encontrar. Eu já fazia anos que não participava de nada", conta.

Assim como centenas de milhares de nicaraguenses, Manuel participou das manifestações de 2018, iniciadas em abril em razão da insatisfação com as reformas no sistema de previdência social. Ao longo dos meses, os protestos evoluíram e passaram a exigir a renúncia de Ortega e Murillo.

Mas, após a repressão violenta às manifestações, que, segundo dados da Comissão Interamericana de Direitos Humanos (CIDH), deixou pelo menos 328 mortos, Manuel preferiu não se envolver mais.

Ele também não tem antecedentes criminais, conforme apurou a BBC Mundo.

A CIDH contabilizou 328 mortes no contexto dos protestos antigovernamentais de 2018 na Nicarágua — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

"Fico pensando: por que eu estaria fichado? Talvez minhas experiências profissionais tenham sido em espaços que não são bem vistos por eles [o governo], mas não sinto que eu seja alguém importante nem uma peça-chave em nenhum sentido."

Ao sair da Nicarágua, não teve problemas. "Fui embora supertranquilo porque pensei: 'Se forem criar algum problema para mim, vão fazer isso aqui mesmo'. Então aproveitei muito a viagem, visitei nove cidades e correu tudo bem. Tinha me divertido bastante", conta.

No dia em que estava previsto seu voo de volta, no aeroporto de Madri, Manuel não sabia muito bem o que fazer.

Depois de tentar assimilar o que havia acontecido, pegou um trem e voltou para Múrcia, cidade no sudeste da Península Ibérica, onde estavam alguns familiares. Dias depois, decidiu que voltaria à Nicarágua.

"Hoje me arrependo de não ter ficado", confessa.

Alguns familiares e amigos, lembra ele, recomendaram que permanecesse na Espanha e pedisse asilo.

"Eu tinha razões pessoais. Estava tentando ir depois para os Estados Unidos. Também pensei nos meus cachorros. Para muita gente isso pode parecer ridículo, mas meus cachorros e minha gata são como meus filhos", conta.

"Depois pensava nos gastos, no medo de onde iria trabalhar aqui. Aí pensei: e daí se tivesse que limpar mesas? E daí se tivesse que reconstruir minha vida?", continua.

"Mas, naquele momento, senti o peso de já ter uma vida estabelecida na Nicarágua. Minha casa, meus familiares, meu círculo social. Os bens materiais também pesam. Investi tanto dinheiro na minha casa. Fazia pouco tempo que tinha comprado meu carro. Era horrível pensar em tudo o que teria de deixar para trás."

Por meio de familiares na Nicarágua, conseguiu contatos de pessoas que o ajudariam a entrar irregularmente no país a partir de Honduras. Assim, comprou uma passagem.

Nos dias que antecederam o embarque, procurou falar o mínimo possível sobre o que havia acontecido.

Algumas semanas depois, Manuel voltou ao aeroporto de Madri.

"A ansiedade que senti durante toda aquela viagem foi, acho, pior do que a que senti no momento em que me disseram que eu não poderia entrar na Nicarágua", lembra.

"Eu me sentia paranoico. Achava que encontraria sandinistas até mesmo no aeroporto."

Ele desembarcou em Honduras, onde pessoas que o ajudariam a atravessar a fronteira rumo ao seu país o aguardavam.

"Cheguei de madrugada e viajamos durante algumas horas para estarmos na fronteira pela manhã", conta.

No posto fronteiriço, lembra, as pessoas que o acompanhavam organizaram tudo.

"Disse que havia entrado [no país] pelo aeroporto e que precisava que registrassem minha saída. Então, um homem me levou até seu contato na imigração hondurenha e disse: 'Aqui eles só vão carimbar sua saída e depois vamos embora'", relata.

Ele conta que, depois de passar pelo guichê e receber o carimbo que comprovava sua saída de Honduras, em vez de se dirigir ao local onde receberia o carimbo de entrada na Nicarágua, seguiu por um caminho em direção à mata.

Minutos depois, viu-se cercado por plantações de café e banana, avistando ao longe algumas casinhas de zinco.

Manuel havia se preparado para caminhar com conforto: vestia jeans, camiseta e tênis, e carregava uma bolsa com seus documentos.

Além do guia, era acompanhado por alguns rapazes contratados por seus contatos para ajudá-lo a carregar as malas.

"Na verdade, fui um irresponsável. Estava levando uma bolsa, uma mala de mão e duas malas grandes, como se estivesse viajando normalmente", reflete agora.

Ele não quis deixar para trás os vinhos, presuntos e alfajores que havia comprado para os amigos e familiares.

Disseram a ele que o percurso normalmente levava cerca de 20 minutos, mas que havia chovido muito na noite anterior.

"Tive azar. O lugar por onde eu ia atravessar é como os fundos de uma fazenda: estava com muita lama, meus pés afundavam, eu escorregava e precisava me agarrar aos galhos das árvores. Queimei as mãos com a seiva da bananeira", recorda.

Ele conta que o trajeto pareceu mais longo por causa do cansaço e da paranoia. Praticamente acabara de cruzar o Atlântico em um voo de dez horas, ao qual se somaram mais cinco horas de carro até chegar à fronteira.

Era dia, ele sentia que estava sendo perseguido e qualquer barulho fazia seu coração disparar.

"Eu estava em território estrangeiro. Honduras não é exatamente o país mais pacífico da América Central, e qualquer coisa poderia acontecer. Eu estava me expondo", recorda.

"Então voltei a pensar se tinha sido uma boa ideia retornar. Mas já havia gastado mais de mil dólares em outra passagem, então comecei a chorar e disse a mim mesmo: 'Bom, meu Deus, vou continuar'."

E continuou seguindo por entre as árvores, parando e se abaixando quando seus guias indicavam.

"'Como isso pode estar acontecendo comigo?', disse a mim mesmo, chorando, na primeira vez que me sentei. Nem sequer tenho multas de trânsito, nunca tive problemas com ninguém. Nunca na minha vida tive problemas com a polícia, nunca houve uma denúncia contra mim, uma queixa, nada, nem o menor problema", lembra.

"Isso dá a sensação de que estão tratando você como um criminoso. É tão humilhante. Você se sente como se não valesse nada", afirma, com a voz embargada.

Depois de cerca de meia hora, conseguiu avistar a estrada. Já estava na Nicarágua e, a poucos metros dali, um familiar o aguardava em uma caminhonete.

"Quando o vi, o abracei e comecei a chorar novamente. Disse a ele que jamais imaginei que ficaria tão feliz em vê-lo."

Mas voltar à Nicarágua não significou recuperar a vida que tinha antes de partir.

Nas primeiras semanas, ele teve dificuldade para dormir. Acordava de madrugada, assustado, pensando que a polícia poderia aparecer e arrombar o portão de sua casa. Ficava observando as imagens das câmeras de segurança em busca de qualquer sinal estranho.

"Passei um mês trancado em casa", conta.

Depois, mudou de academia e passou a frequentar uma mais perto de casa. Começou a pedir comida por delivery para não sair a restaurantes e a evitar lugares muito movimentados. "Optei por uma vida mais isolada."

Manuel voltou à Nicarágua, mas não à vida que tinha antes de partir — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

Yader Valdivia, coordenador de documentação do Coletivo de Direitos Humanos Nicaragua Nunca Más, prefere não revelar quantos casos de pessoas que entraram no país após terem tido a entrada negada a organização já contabilizou, mas afirma que foram identificadas duas modalidades.

Por um lado, "alguns empresários tiveram que escrever cartas ao governo liderado por Daniel Ortega e Rosario Murillo, pedindo desculpas e solicitando autorização para entrar no país. Posteriormente, tiveram que pagar quantias entre US$ 6 mil e US$ 9 mil. Depende do caso, não há um valor fixo, e sabemos que essas extorsões vêm de diferentes setores", relata.

"Também há pessoas que entraram irregularmente para viver clandestinamente na Nicarágua, porque o exílio também não é uma opção para elas", afirma.

Ele deixou o país novamente para pedir asilo

Depois de passar vários meses "em uma espécie de limbo", Manuel decidiu deixar a Nicarágua novamente, da mesma forma como havia entrado: de maneira irregular.

"Eu não podia estar legalmente no meu próprio país, e meu maior medo era ser detido. Não queria viver assim", admite.

Hoje, ele está novamente na Espanha, onde solicitou asilo político.

"Desta vez, vim com o plano de recomeçar minha vida. Dói ter deixado minha família e minhas coisas para vir em direção ao desconhecido. É uma tristeza", afirma.

"Mas aqui me sinto mais tranquilo, fora de perigo, embora me revolte não poder estar na Nicarágua."

Manuel queria permanecer em seu país, continuar com a vida que construiu e que conhece.

Embora, no fundo, quando ouviu naquele aeroporto que não poderia mais voltar, tenha percebido que aquela Nicarágua já havia ficado para trás.

articles.title: Mosquitos geneticamente modificados reduzem dengue em 69% em BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo realizado em Belo Horizonte identificou redução de 69% nas infecções por dengue e chikungunya em bairros que receberam mosquitos portadores da bactéria "Wolbachia".
articles.summary: Estudo com 5.700 crianças em Belo Horizonte comprova que mosquitos geneticamente modificados com a bactéria Wolbachia reduzem em 69% os casos de dengue e chikungunya.
articles.body:
Pesquisadores divulgaram neste sábado (21) um estudo feito com mais de 5.700 crianças moradoras de Belo Horizonte (MG). A pesquisa mostrou que aquelas, que moravam em regiões onde circulava um tipo especial de mosquito Aedes aegypti, tinham menos chances de contrair dengue ou chikungunya.

A pesquisa acompanhou mais de 5.700 crianças e apresenta novas evidências de que a criação e a disseminação de mosquitos incapazes de transmitir esses vírus podem ser uma estratégia eficaz de combate às doenças .

A abordagem oferece uma alternativa à dependência exclusiva de inseticidas e de medidas para evitar picadas.

Nos bairros onde foram introduzidos mosquitos portadores da bactéria Wolbachia , os pesquisadores identificaram uma redução de aproximadamente 69% nas infecções por dengue e chikungunya entre crianças em idade escolar, na comparação com bairros semelhantes.

Mosquito-da-Dengue (Aedes aegypti) — Foto: eeuforiee / iNaturalist

O efeito se manteve mesmo durante o grave surto de dengue registrado no Brasil em 2024, afirmou o médico Sri Edupuganti, da Universidade Emory, integrante da equipe internacional de pesquisa.

Os resultados foram apresentados em uma reunião da Sociedade Americana de Medicina Tropical e Higiene.

"Isso é realmente empolgante", afirmou o médico David Hamer, especialista em saúde global da Universidade de Boston, que não participou do estudo brasileiro. Ele prevê que a ampliação do uso de mosquitos com Wolbachia , combinada às medidas já existentes de combate às doenças transmitidas por esses insetos, poderá "reduzir a dengue a níveis muito mais baixos" em diversos lugares.

A nova pesquisa foi divulgada em um momento em que a Flórida enfrenta um surto incomumente grande da doença. O episódio parece ser o maior registrado em qualquer estado americano desde pelo menos a década de 1940.

Normalmente, nos Estados Unidos continentais, a dengue é identificada principalmente em pessoas que viajaram para outros países. Mas, até esta sexta-feira, autoridades de saúde da Flórida haviam contabilizado mais de 650 casos contraídos localmente. Cerca de três quartos deles foram registrados no condado de Hillsborough, onde fica a cidade de Tampa.

Fora dos Estados Unidos, a organização sem fins lucrativos World Mosquito Program foi pioneira no desenvolvimento da estratégia com a bactéria Wolbachia.

Os cientistas criam mosquitos portadores de um tipo de bactéria chamado Wolbachia. Ela é inofensiva para os seres humanos e comum em diversas espécies de insetos, mas não costuma estar presente no Aedes aegypti, mosquito transmissor da dengue.

A bactéria reduz significativamente a capacidade dos mosquitos de transmitir determinados vírus. As fêmeas transmitem a bactéria aos descendentes. Assim, a liberação de uma quantidade suficiente de insetos especialmente criados — machos e fêmeas — em uma determinada região permite que a Wolbachia se estabeleça gradualmente na população local de mosquitos.

Testes de campo e outros estudos realizados na Indonésia e em diferentes países já demonstraram que a estratégia pode reduzir significativamente os diagnósticos de dengue.

Mas, como pessoas com sintomas leves podem não receber um diagnóstico, a nova pesquisa, realizada em Belo Horizonte, foi além. Os pesquisadores analisaram amostras de sangue em busca de sinais de infecção por dengue, chikungunya ou zika.

O estudo, que durou quatro anos, comparou crianças que viviam em bairros onde foram adotadas as mesmas medidas de controle de mosquitos, incluindo o uso de inseticidas. Metade das áreas foi escolhida aleatoriamente para receber a liberação de mosquitos portadores da Wolbachia.

O número de casos de zika foi muito baixo para que os pesquisadores conseguissem calcular se os mosquitos especiais tiveram algum efeito sobre a doença.

articles.title: Menino de 2 anos morre após se afogar em caixa d'água no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo familiar, João Vitor de Brito Paula foi levado ao hospital, mas não resistiu. Caso ocorreu em Epitaciolândia na sexta (20).
articles.summary: Segundo familiar, João Vitor de Brito Paula foi levado ao hospital, mas não resistiu. Caso ocorreu em Epitaciolândia na sexta (20).
articles.body:
João Vitor de Brito Paula chegou a ser socorrido, mas morreu no hospital — Foto: Reprodução

Um menino de dois anos, identificado como João Vitor de Brito Paula, morreu após se afogar em uma caixa d'água no bairro Satel, em Epitaciolândia , no interior do Acre, nessa sexta-feira (20).

Segundo um familiar que preferiu não ser identificado, a criança saiu de casa por volta das 9h e seguiu em direção aos fundos do imóvel, onde havia uma caixa d'água próxima a um pequeno barranco.

O menino teria caído dentro do reservatório e permanecido submerso por cerca de 30 a 40 minutos. No momento do acidente, a mãe da criança estava trabalhando, e o menino estava sob os cuidados das irmãs, conforme informou a família.

O parente contou que estava de plantão no hospital quando João Vitor foi levado para atendimento. Ele mesmo recebeu a criança e a carregou nos braços até o pronto-socorro. O atendimento ocorreu no Hospital Regional do Alto Acre, em Brasiléia, município vizinho a Epitaciolândia.

"Ele chegou para mim no hospital já sem vida, mas, como os paramédicos tinham que fazer o procedimento, eles fizeram. Tiraram quase meio litro de água dentro dele. Foi coisa rápida, foi muito rápido. Os médicos do município fizeram todos os procedimentos, só lamento mesmo que ele chegou a óbito", relatou ao g1 .

A morte da criança causou comoção no município. A prefeitura publicou uma nota de pesar nas redes sociais, na qual manifestou solidariedade aos familiares e amigos. ( Confira na íntegra no final da reportagem )

"Neste momento de dor, a administração municipal se solidariza e presta sinceras condolências aos familiares e amigos, rogando a Deus que conforte seus corações e conceda força para enfrentar essa irreparável perda", diz a publicação.

Leia na íntegra a nota da Prefeitura de Epitaciolândia

Prefeitura de Epitaciolândia, na pessoa do Prefeito Sérgio Mesquita, manifesta o mais profundo pesar pelo falecimento de João Vitor.

Neste momento de dor, a administração municipal se solidariza e presta sinceras condolências aos familiares e amigos, rogando a Deus que conforte seus corações e conceda força para enfrentar essa irreparável perda.

"Este é o meu consolo no meu sofrimento: A tua promessa dá-me vida.”

articles.title: Shiv Nadar tops philanthropy list for fifth year; India's richest donate Rs 11,554 crore
articles.summary: MUMBAI: HCL founder Shiv Nadar and his family have retained the title of India's most generous philanthropists for the fifth consecutive year, donating Rs
articles.body: MUMBAI: HCL founder Shiv Nadar and his family have retained the title of India's most generous philanthropists for the fifth consecutive year, donating Rs 2,593 crore in 2025-26, or an average of Rs 7.1 crore every day, according to the EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List 2026 released on Friday.The report, now in its 13th edition, shows that 219 philanthropists collectively donated Rs 11,554 crore during the financial year, an increase of 11% over the Rs 10,380 crore recorded last year. The number of philanthropists on the list has risen from 192 to 219, while new entrants have nearly quadrupled from 12 to 45.Gautam Adani and his family climbed three places to the second position after more than doubling their contribution to Rs 877 crore, an increase of 127%. The Bajaj family retained third place with Rs 632 crore, followed by Mukesh Ambani and family at Rs 620 crore.Nandan Nilekani ranked fifth with Rs 380 crore, followed by Kumar Mangalam Birla and family (Rs 366 crore), Cyrus and Adar Poonawalla (Rs 336 crore), Sudhir and Samir Mehta (Rs 334 crore), Ranjan Pai and family (Rs 219 crore) and Rohini Nilekani (Rs 215 crore).Education continued to attract the largest share of philanthropic contributions, receiving Rs 4,188 crore, accounting for 36% of the total donations. As many as 200 of the 219 philanthropists supported education, while it was the primary cause for 95 donors.Healthcare emerged as another major beneficiary, with donations rising 82% to Rs 1,768 crore. Contributions towards arts, culture and heritage stood at Rs 1,377 crore, while environment and sustainability attracted Rs 813 crore, an increase of 86%.Rohini Nilekani emerged as India's most generous woman philanthropist with a contribution of Rs 215 crore, followed by Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw (Rs 93 crore) and Anu Aga and family (Rs 78 crore), Bina Shah of Harish and Bina Shah Foundation (Rs 77.5 crore). The number of women philanthropists increased from 24 to 29.Mumbai continued to lead the country in the number of philanthropists, with 64 individuals, seven more than last year. New Delhi followed with 41 and Bengaluru with 20. However, New Delhi topped the list in terms of donation value at Rs 3,168 crore, marginally ahead of Mumbai's Rs 3,007 crore.The report also highlighted the growing participation of self-made entrepreneurs. Of the 219 philanthropists, 125 were self-made, accounting for 57% of the list and 65% of the total donations.Among the new entrants were Motilal Oswal Financial Services co-founders Raamdeo Agrawal and Motilal Oswal, who contributed Rs 120 crore and Rs 119 crore respectively. New York-based Chandrika and Ranjan Tandon donated Rs 100 crore towards establishing a School of Artificial Intelligence at IIM Ahmedabad.Last year, India overtook China with more donors giving Rs 100 crore or more, this year, China has 30 donors versus 19 Indians who donated more than Rs 100 crore.Despite the growing number of donors, philanthropic contributions remained concentrated among a relatively small group. The top 10 philanthropists accounted for Rs 6,572 crore, or 57% of all donations, while just 19 individuals who donated Rs 100 crore or more contributed 68% of the total.Naghma Mulla, CEO of EdelGive Foundation, said the growing number of new entrants reflected a shift in how wealthy Indians viewed philanthropy. "In 2014, a year after we started publishing the list, we had 50 philanthropists on it. This year, we have 219. That is a 338% increase," she said.Anas Rahman Junaid, founder and chief researcher of Hurun India, said India's growing wealth was opening a new chapter in philanthropy, with entrepreneurs increasingly choosing to give back while continuing to build their businesses.The report, however, also flagged a concern in corporate social responsibility spending. articles.title: Anthropic mathematician claims to solve 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis with Claude: What is the $1 million maths puzzle
articles.summary: An Anthropic mathematician has claimed to have developed a proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis with the help of the company's artificial
articles.body: An Anthropic mathematician has claimed to have developed a proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis with the help of the company's artificial intelligence model Claude, potentially marking a landmark moment for AI-assisted mathematical research.Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced on Friday that he believed he had solved the famous mathematical problem, which concerns the distribution of prime numbers and has remained unresolved since 1859. The proposed proof also addresses the generalised Riemann hypothesis, a broader version of the original conjecture.The claim has drawn attention from leading mathematicians, although the proof still needs wider independent scrutiny and a deeper understanding of its mathematical reasoning. James Maynard, the Regius Professor of Mathematics at the University of Oxford and a 2022 Fields Medal winner, expressed optimism about the result.“If this fully checks out, it is clearly a historic milestone in mathematics, establishing one of the great mysteries of the subject,” Maynard told IBM Think in an interview. “This result really stands out, even in the context of all the recent AI breakthroughs.”Alpöge shared the proposed proof in Lean, a programming language and proof assistant that checks mathematical arguments step by step. The format allows researchers to examine whether each part of the reasoning follows logically, although verifying the computer-checked argument and understanding the ideas behind it are separate challenges.In a statement posted on his website, Alpöge wrote: “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis.”What is the Riemann hypothesis?First proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers, which are divisible only by themselves and one. Examples include 2, 3 and 5.Although prime numbers appear to occur irregularly along the number line, the Riemann hypothesis predicts that their distribution follows a deeper mathematical pattern. Proving it would resolve one of the most enduring questions in number theory and provide a stronger understanding of the structure of numbers.The problem is among the seven Millennium Prize Problems identified by the Clay Mathematics Institute. Each carries a prize of $1 million for a correct solution.Alpöge's announcement follows a series of AI-assisted advances in mathematics, with large language models increasingly being used to explore complex conjectures and theoretical problems. The latest claim, if verified, would represent a major step beyond earlier results that established the predicted pattern for only a proportion of certain mathematical values.Why the proposed proof mattersYouness Lamzouri, a professor of mathematics at the University of Lorraine in France, said the proposed result would go substantially further than an earlier AI-assisted breakthrough.Previous work had established that at least 67.25% of a particular set of mathematical values followed the pattern predicted by the Riemann hypothesis. The new claim, if correct, would establish that all of them follow the pattern without exception.Lamzouri, who developed a shorter proof of the earlier result without AI, said the latest announcement had left him astonished.“I don’t have words to describe what I am feeling right now. I am just in awe,” he said. “If this claim happens to be true, it will be a huge achievement.”However, he cautioned that checking the computer-generated proof would only be the first step. Mathematicians would also need to understand the reasoning and ideas behind it before accepting its broader implications.“Mathematics is mainly about understanding why something is true,” he said. “We need to understand the ideas in the proof well enough to explain them, teach them and build on them to extend human knowledge.”Hector Pasten, a mathematician at the Pontifical Catholic University of Chile, said a verified and understood proof could establish connections between different areas of mathematics.“If the proof is correct and understood, this completes a dictionary between different branches of math where the connections were only partial,” Pasten said, describing it as “something like a Rosetta Stone.”Carlo Pagano, a professor at Concordia University in Quebec and a visiting researcher at Google DeepMind, also pointed to the potential for new research directions."If true, even from a first high level scan of the summary of the proposed argument, it is very plausible to me that the new ideas in the proof will open up brand new avenues of thinking in number theory and have an immense impact beside the obviously extremely influential result in itself," Pagano said.Mathematicians face task of verifying the resultThe use of Lean gives researchers a way to check the logical validity of the proposed proof, but experts have stressed that this does not automatically explain the mathematical ideas that led to the result.Maynard said he was optimistic about the claim but cautioned that independent verification would take time.“I suspect that the proof will turn out to be correct, although even checking the Lean verification will take some time,” he said.He also warned that understanding the underlying mathematics could prove more difficult than checking the computer verification.“So somewhat frustratingly, it looks like it will require quite a lot of work to really gain this understanding,” Maynard said.Andrew Sutherland, a mathematician at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, said he had independently compiled Alpöge's result in Lean and described the development as a historic moment.“This is indeed an historic moment,” Sutherland said. “The world has changed.... I know there will be a wide range of reactions in our community, but to me this is a human triumph, and a day for celebration.”Sutherland said the achievement should also be viewed in the context of the human work behind the development of Lean, large language models and centuries of mathematical research.“There is much work to be done to understand the mathematical details of the proof,” he said. “And I can’t wait to dig into them. But perhaps the single most important step in the proof was building a machine that can think.”A turning point for AI-assisted mathematics?Alpöge's claim comes after a year of growing attention on the ability of AI models to tackle difficult mathematical problems. He had earlier attracted attention in July after sharing a Claude-generated solution to the Jacobian conjecture. He was also involved in a September controversy surrounding an OpenAI mathematical result related to the Navier-Stokes problem.If the Riemann hypothesis proof is independently verified and its reasoning understood, it could mark a major advance in the use of AI for mathematical discovery. The result would not necessarily have immediate practical applications, but it could reshape research in number theory and deepen understanding of connections across mathematics.For now, the central question is whether the proposed proof withstands independent examination. Even if the computer verification holds, mathematicians will need to establish why the argument works and what new avenues it opens.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: An Air Niugini aircraft carrying 146 people from Hong Kong to Papua New Guinea made an emergency landing in the southern Philippines on Saturday after its warning system indicated a possible fire in one of its engines, aviation officials said.All 137 passengers and nine crew members were safe, with no injuries reported, according to news agency AP. The passengers and crew evacuated the Boeing 767-383ER using emergency slides after the aircraft diverted from its scheduled route and landed at Davao International Airport, the Civil Aviation Authority of the Philippines said.According to Eric Apolonio, spokesperson for the aviation authority, the pilots received an indication of possible sparks or fire in the aircraft's right engine. They followed safety procedures and requested permission to make an unscheduled landing in Davao shortly after midnight.Apolonio did not provide further details but said the investigation would also include statements from the pilots.Passengers and crew members were taken to the airport terminal, where they received assistance and hotel accommodation. There were no immediate reports of damage to the aircraft.The Davao airport temporarily suspended other flights to allow emergency teams to respond to the incident. articles.title: A Maine couple installed giant metal roosters outside their home to comfort their six-year-old daughter; after the town treated the figures as business advertising and imposed $1,700 in fines, they filed a federal lawsuit
articles.summary: What began as a way to make the daily journey to school less difficult for a young girl has turned into a legal battle over free speech, disability rights
articles.body: What began as a way to make the daily journey to school less difficult for a young girl has turned into a legal battle over free speech, disability rights and the meaning of public art in a small Maine town. David and Sara LeBlanc, residents of Ogunquit, Maine, have filed a federal lawsuit against the town after officials repeatedly penalised them for displaying large metal rooster sculptures outside their home. The couple maintains that the decorations were put up for their six-year-old daughter, Pyper, who has autism and has a particular fondness for roosters. However, town officials classified the figures as commercial advertising for the family’s restaurant, the Omelette Factory. According to reports by the Associated Press, Maine Public and the Portland Press Herald, the dispute has been unfolding for months, with the family now challenging the town’s enforcement of its sign regulations in court.The story began in May 2025, when the LeBlancs brought home a six-foot-tall tin rooster. Pyper had always been fascinated by the bird, and her parents noticed that having the sculpture outside made her daily school routine easier. For the young girl, the rooster gradually became part of a familiar ritual. She would spend time near it while waiting for her school bus and return to it after coming home. What started as a single decoration eventually grew into a collection of around two dozen sculptures, although the family says it generally displayed no more than eight at a time.The figures were also decorated during different seasons and holidays, becoming a distinctive feature outside the family’s property. However, the arrangement attracted the attention of local authorities because the LeBlancs’ home is connected to their breakfast restaurant, the Omelette Factory. Officials argued that the rooster sculptures effectively advertised the business and therefore fell under Ogunquit’s municipal sign regulations.In April 2026, the family received a notice directing them to remove the unpermitted displays. The dispute subsequently escalated, with the couple receiving multiple fines. WMTW reported that the penalties amounted to $1,700, while the Portland Press Herald reported that the total had exceeded $2,000.The family also sought an accommodation under disability-related provisions. The town granted a variance allowing two roosters to remain, but stipulated that they had to be incorporated into a railing attached to the residence. Since the property did not have the specified railing, the couple instead chained the sculptures to posts near their entrance. Officials subsequently issued further citations.The disagreement eventually left the family with little choice but to remove the original display. However, the sculptures did not disappear from the neighbourhood. Friends, neighbours and local businesses began taking in the roosters and displaying them on their own properties as a gesture of support for Pyper. The decorations have since become a recognisable symbol of community solidarity, with residents and supporters elsewhere also purchasing similar figures.According to the Institute for Justice, the legal organisation representing the family, other property owners have been allowed to display identical rooster decorations without facing similar enforcement action. The organisation filed the federal lawsuit on November 16, arguing that the town’s interpretation and application of its sign code violate the family’s First Amendment rights. The complaint also raises concerns about whether officials can determine the meaning of a decorative object based on the identity of its owner or its proximity to a business.The LeBlancs are seeking a court declaration that the enforcement was unconstitutional, along with an order preventing the town from issuing further penalties over the sculptures. The legal challenge is currently listed as an active case. The dispute has also drawn comparisons with a separate First Amendment case involving a bakery mural in Conway, New Hampshire. In 2025, a judge ruled in favour of a bakery owner after town officials attempted to regulate a mural painted by high school students, which featured doughnuts and other baked goods.For Pyper, however, the controversy has a more personal dimension. Her parents have said that seeing other people display the roosters brings her happiness, even as she struggles to understand why the town objected to something that had become so important to her. Meanwhile, Ogunquit’s town officials have not publicly provided a response to the newly filed lawsuit, leaving the disagreement over the sculptures’ legal status to be settled in court.You use AI every day. articles.title: Over 32 years, Colombian mason Santiago Rojas built a stone house for his wife Gloria, turning a modest home into La Casa de las Piedritas
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring story of Santiago Rojas, a Colombian mason who dedicated 32 years to transforming his wife's dream into reality by constructing La Casa de las Piedritas, a unique stone house filled with love and history.
articles.body: In Envigado, Colombia, Santiago Rojas spent 32 years transforming an old family property into a house covered with stones. Known as Casa Santiago y Gloria or La Casa de las Piedritas, the home became a reflection of a childhood dream and a promise he made to his wife, Gloria Ochoa. Rojas added stones to the property every day gradually, giving the distinctive appearance that attracted visitors from different places. The house was more than 150 years old, according to the account featured by Travel Is Life. Its transformation began after Rojas fulfilled a wish he had carried since childhood: buying the property from his aunt.A childhood dream became a home for GloriaRojas was born in San José, Envigado. The house that later turned out to be La Casa de las Piedritas belonged to his aunt. He often assured her as a child that one day, when he grew up and earned money, he would buy that house. He finally made the dream come true and the house became the fulfilment of a promise he had made as a child. Rojas purchased the land and gifted it to Gloria, his wife, before starting the long work on its transformation. The profile by Gente in 2021 explains the background of the project. It says that Rojas promised Gloria a house made of stones and to bring her a flower each day. Moreover, the stones have their own sentimental value. Every time Rojas visited her and found her door shut, he would throw a stone against the window to show that he was here. Some of the stones have allegedly been preserved and have become part of the house.32 years of adding stones by handThe development of the land was gradual. A 2017 report by Gente described La Casa de las Piedritas as a project that Santiago Rojas had been developing for nearly three decades. He had promised his wife Gloria that he would build her a house made of stones. According to him, he was developing “the most beautiful stone house in the world” for himself and Gloria. Stones turned out to be the main elements of the house. Rojas continued working on his property throughout all those years, turning it into what he was imagining.This work was an example of Rojas’ patience and determination to fulfil the promise. A Gente report published after Rojas’s death in May 2022 also lists the materials used to build the house. In addition to stones, there were cement, adobe, bamboo, cane, tiles, roofing material, construction waste, stained glass and even eyeglass lenses. Rojas was working on all these materials, giving them a special shape.A local attraction built around a personal storyEventually, the house turned into a known attraction in the neighbourhood of San José, Envigado. Tourists were drawn by the unique stone building and the tale of how it was made. Rojas warmly received visitors and enjoyed the attention given to his home. Rojas claimed in an interview with Gente that he was proud that his house had become a landmark because of his dream that came true. Gente reported on May 10, 2022, that Rojas had died. His work was kept in Envigado as a permanent attribute of the neighbourhood culture. La Casa de las Piedritas was constructed based on Rojas’ childhood dream of having a certain house and the promise to build a special place for Gloria. articles.title: Lanzarote opened Europe’s first underwater art museum in 2017 to create an artificial reef; an early survey reported marine biomass up by more than 200%
articles.summary: Discover how Lanzarote's Museo Atlántico, Europe's first underwater art museum, is boosting marine biodiversity by over 200% while combining art and conservation efforts.
articles.body: Most museums ask visitors to keep their voices low and hands to themselves. This one sits under the Atlantic Ocean, and some of its most curious visitors have fins. A Guardian travel gallery from 10 January 2017 covered the opening of Museo Atlántico off Lanzarote, Europe's first underwater art museum. The project was made for people and also for marine life. The sculptures were intended as an artificial reef, and an early survey reported marine biomass up by more than 200%.A museum made for fish as well as people British sculptor Jason deCaires Taylor created this underwater museum. He installed more than 300 works between February and December 2016. The final piece was Human Gyre, a circle of over 200 life-size figures for which local residents and tourists had posed for the cast. The sculptures were made of pH-neutral, inert materials that would suit local marine life and not harm the waters. The project was meant to create a large artificial reef that would attract local fish and increase marine biomass, while also raising awareness about threats to the world's oceans.What the 200% figure really shows The 200% figure was from the earliest sculptures sitting in the water for less than a year when the museum opened. It was a hopeful sign, but it wasn’t the result of a long-term study. Instead, it was based on numbers released in the project's opening announcement. Biomass is the total weight of all living things in an area. A higher number can mean more fish, bigger fish, or even more small creatures growing on the structures. However, it cannot tell us whether that life was newly produced or simply moved in from nearby. For years, scientists have debated that difference.Fish do settle on the new reefs in the Canary IslandsEarlier research from the same island group shed light on this issue. In a 2002 article titled ‘Observations on fish colonization and predation on two artificial reefs in the Canary Islands’, published in the ICES Journal of Marine Science, Herrera-Pérez and colleagues studied fish on two artificial reefs over several years using visual counts. They observed 53 fish species across the two reefs. The isolated oceanic reef was associated with fish that live on rocky seabeds, as well as a large seasonal influx of small open-water fish. This study suggested that fish could colonise newly built structures in these waters. It did not include Museo Atlántico and therefore couldn't confirm what exactly happened there.Do artificial reefs create life or just attract it? The real question is how much life an artificial reef does add. A 2025 Fish and Fisheries review looked at the evidence. The authors, including Raymond Czaja Jr., noted that artificial reefs are often assumed to increase fish production. But their search turned up only 12 studies that measured how much new animal biomass the reef produced, and only three of those had a control site. All three recorded greater production at the artificial reefs, but the team concluded three studies were too few to make a broad conclusion.A hopeful start, not the last wordSo what does this mean for Lanzarote? The sculptures gave the seabed new structures where fish and other marine life can find a home. The project also announced an early increase in biomass. Fish are known to colonise new reefs in the Canary Islands, so early gains are possible. But the rise measured in less than a year isn’t enough to show whether the reef added new life or just brought fish from somewhere else. Several independent surveys over many years might be needed to show lasting benefits. However, Museo Atlántico shows how art and conservation can work together.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Will find way forward through dialogue': Amit Shah assures Arunachal locals amid Siang dam protests
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah, who is visiting Arunachal Pradesh amid protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah, who is visiting Arunachal Pradesh amid protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), assured locals on Saturday that the Centre would protect their traditions, culture and religious beliefs.Also Read | Shah to visit Arunachal tomorrow amid protests over Siang dam"I am aware of the sentiments and apprehensions of the people of Siang region, and I have come to Arunachal Pradesh to address your concerns directly," Shah said at the Police Training Centre in Banderdewa, near state capital Itanagar.Acknowledging that some of the concerns raised were "significant", Shah assured residents that the government was aware of the aspirations of local communities."I want to assure my brothers and sisters from Siang that we will find a way forward through positive dialogue ... You need not worry about it. The government and I have the same respect you have for the local culture. We will move forward without compromising the traditions, culture and religion of this place," he added.The home minister, whose remarks mark his first public statement on the issue, urged people to engage with the Arunachal Pradesh government and convey their concerns to the Union home ministry through the state administration.Shah's assurance comes amid continued opposition to the proposed mega dam from sections of the indigenous Adi community, particularly residents of Siang and Upper Siang districts. They have expressed concerns over its possible impact on their ancestral lands, villages, livelihood, environment and cultural identity.What is the proposed Siang river projectThe project, proposed on the Siang River, is considered strategically important by the Centre, particularly in view of China's plans to develop a massive hydropower project on the upper reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet. The river enters India as the Siang before flowing into Assam as the Brahmaputra.The project is envisaged not only as a major source of hydroelectric power but also as a strategic intervention to strengthen India's energy and water security. It is expected to help regulate river flows, besides providing Arunachal Pradesh with opportunities for revenue generation, infrastructure development and employment.However, indigenous organisations and local residents have questioned the need for such a massive project, citing the fragile ecology of the Siang Valley and the possible consequences of large-scale construction in a seismically sensitive region.They have also alleged that adequate public consultation has not taken place and demanded greater transparency in the ongoing pre-feasibility report exercise.For many Adi families, the Siang River is not merely a source of livelihood but is closely linked to their history, traditional beliefs and cultural practices.Protests against the project have intensified in recent months, with indigenous groups demanding that the government reconsider the proposal and ensure that the concerns of the affected communities are addressed before proceeding further.(With PTI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US next aircraft carrier to honour Pearl Harbor hero, Navy rejects name change to Trump
articles.summary: Donald Trump may be getting a battleship named after him, but he will not get his name on America's next aircraft carrier.
articles.body: Donald Trump may be getting a battleship named after him, but he will not get his name on America's next aircraft carrier.The US Navy has ruled out renaming its next Ford-class carrier after the president, confirming that the warship will retain the name USS Doris Miller, honouring the Black American sailor who became a hero during Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941.The confirmation comes after months of speculation over a possible name change, with reports in August suggesting that navy officials had discussed renaming the carrier after Trump. The proposal would have replaced the name of Doris Miller, whose bravery during the December 7, 1941, attack on Pearl Harbor made him one of the most celebrated figures in US naval history.The Navy has now put those reports to rest. A spokesperson for acting navy secretary Hung Cao told CNN, "There is no intention to change the name of the USS Doris Miller."The statement effectively rules out the reported proposal and confirms that the next Ford-class aircraft carrier will continue to carry the name of the World War II hero.But why was the carrier's name being reconsidered in the first place? According to CNN's August report, navy officials had held internal discussions about renaming the vessel after Trump. The discussions reportedly came amid a broader push to revisit the navy's ship-naming guidelines, with some officials favouring names of US presidents and senior military leaders for aircraft carriers.The proposal, however, would have meant dropping the name of a sailor whose actions during one of the most defining moments in American military history earned him national recognition.Doris 'Dorie' Miller was serving aboard the USS West Virginia when Japanese forces launched their surprise attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941. Despite having no formal training in operating anti-aircraft guns, Miller took control of one and fired at Japanese aircraft while helping evacuate wounded sailors, including his commanding officer.Miller's bravery earned him the Navy Cross in 1942, making him the first African American sailor to receive the decoration. His recognition was particularly significant at a time when the US navy maintained racial segregation and Black sailors were largely assigned to service roles rather than combat positions.Miller was later killed in November 1943 when a Japanese submarine torpedoed the aircraft carrier USS Liscome Bay during the Battle of Makin.The Navy's decision comes as Trump is already pursuing plans for a new class of warships bearing his name.In December 2025, the president announced the proposed Trump-class battleships as part of his 'Golden Fleet' initiative, with the first vessel expected to be named USS Defiant.The plan would make Trump the namesake of an entirely new class of US navy warships, even as the Navy has ruled out putting his name on the next Ford-class aircraft carrier.You use AI every day. articles.title: IndusInd Bank seizes and auctions UP man's truck over just Rs 43,000 in unpaid EMIs; National Consumer Commission orders bank to pay Rs 7.7 lakh compensation with interest
articles.summary: RAMPUR: A resident of Rampur district in UP had got a truck financed from IndusInd Bank in 2018.
articles.body: RAMPUR: A resident of Rampur district in UP had got a truck financed from IndusInd Bank in 2018. During the Covid-19 pandemic, he could not pay the EMIs, and the bank got his truck lifted and auctioned over an immediate default of Rs 43,000.The man contested the bank’s action from the district to the national commission and finally got relief. On November 17, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission ruled in his favour and ordered the bank to pay him Rs 7.7 lakh — the insured declared value (IDV) of the truck — with interest within eight weeks.The NCDRC panel, presided over by Justice Sudip Ahluwalia and member Justice Anoop Kumar Mendiratta, was considering a revision petition filed by IndusInd Bank against the January 24, 2024, order of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Uttar Pradesh.The state commission had held the bank deficient in service and directed it to pay compensation of Rs 20 lakh to the truck owner while setting aside the March 13, 2023, order of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Rampur.The DCDRC had held that the bank was entitled to repossess and auction the vehicle in terms of the loan agreement upon default in repayment of instalments and that no deficiency in service was established.Relief by the National CommissionWhile considering the revision petition filed by IndusInd Bank, the NCDRC said, “We are in agreement with the State Commission that seizure and sale of the vehicle on account of outstanding payment of only Rs 43,000/- was unconscionable on the part of the Financer.But for inexplicable reasons, the State Commission has awarded the Respondent a composite compensation of Rs.20.00 Lakhs which is far in excess of the Respondent’s own claim of actual IDV Rs 7,69,500.To that extent, the impugned Order would certainly appear to be unreasonable and uncalled for. The Revision Petition is, therefore, partly allowed after modifying the impugned Order to the extent that the Petitioner/Financer shall pay an amount of Rs 7,69,500/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the Original Complaint,” the panel said.It added that if the payment was not made within eight weeks from the date of passing of the order, any outstanding amount would attract interest at 9% per annum.The background of the loan and defaultThe case originated when Rampur man Istekhar Khan approached IndusInd Bank on November 29, 2018, to get a Tata truck financed for a loan of Rs 4,56,880.The loan was to be repaid in 36 monthly instalments. Khan had deposited Rs 3,86,796 till January 20, 2020. In February 2020, he suffered from jaundice, which disrupted the payment of instalments, and an outstanding amount of more than Rs 1 lakh became due.In March 2020, while returning from Bihar, his vehicle was seized by the bank, and Khan was directed to deposit Rs 43,000 immediately.The borrower offered to deposit Rs 20,000, but the bank did not accept the offer and refused to release the vehicle. The bank then auctioned the vehicle and informed Khan that the recovered amount had been deposited in the loan account and that there was still a shortfall of Rs 32,000, which he was supposed to clear.Khan paid the outstanding amount on March 23, 2021, and subsequently, the loan account was closed.Loanee approaches the Consumer CommissionAggrieved by the bank's action, Khan filed an application with the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Rampur, seeking relief on account of 'deficiency in service' by the bank, which had auctioned his vehicle worth over Rs 7.7 lakh for a default of merely Rs 43,000.The district commission held that the bank had failed to establish that Khan was engaged in the business of purchasing and driving vehicles and, therefore, should be excluded from the definition of a 'Consumer'.It further said that even the closure of the loan account would not affect the 'Consumer' status of the complainant. However, on the question of repossession and auction, it held that the bank was entitled to take possession of the vehicle and auction it in terms of the loan agreement upon default in payment of instalments.It also held that Khan had failed to establish, through expert evidence, that the vehicle had been auctioned at an inadequate price and concluded that the bank had acted in accordance with the terms of the loan agreement and that no deficiency in service was established.Appeal filed before State CommissionUnhappy with the DCDRC's order, Khan filed an appeal before the State Commission in Lucknow on June 7, 2023. State commission president Justice Ashok Kumar ruled in favour of the appellant and said, “I do not agree with the contention of the District Commission that even after taking the vehicle in its custody the Bank auctioned it due to non-deposit of the loan amount whereas it is clear from the records that due to illness and Corona, the financial condition of the Respondent had become miserable,” the commission said.It noted that Khan had deposited Rs 3,86,796 by January 20, 2020, and had outstanding dues of more than Rs 1 lakh when his vehicle was seized.“The Respondent was ready to deposit Rs.20 thousand but the Petitioner did not accept the request and thus a vehicle worth Rs.769500 was confiscated due to non-deposit of only Rs.43000.00 and the vehicle purchased for livelihood was auctioned which was deficiency in services,” the commission held, ordering the bank to pay compensation of Rs 20 lakh.Bank approaches National Commission against SCDRC orderThe bank approached the National Consumer Commission with a revision petition, seeking to quash the January 24, 2024, order of the state commission. In its written version, the bank took the stand that an amount of Rs 4,56,880 had been sanctioned to Khan for purchasing the vehicle in question.He was required to repay the amount of Rs 4,56,880 along with interest of Rs 1,14,860 and an insurance premium of Rs 75,000 in monthly instalments.“An amount of Rs.2,49,244/- was irregularly deposited till Jan 20, 2020 and as such there was an outstanding amount against him. Due to such default and lack of financial discipline in paying the installments, the vehicle was seized on March 17, 2020 and Khan was orally informed but he did not show any interest in paying the outstanding amount. Subsequently, the vehicle was auctioned for the purpose of recovery of the balance loan amount,” the bank's counsel said.On the other hand, Khan’s counsel supported the order passed by the State Commission and submitted that the vehicle had been purchased for Rs 9,25,000 by his client for earning his livelihood, and an additional expenditure of Rs 2,15,000 had also been incurred on it.“The vehicle valued at more than Rs.9,00,000/- was auctioned for peanuts by the Bank thereby depriving my client of his livelihood and opportunity to pay back the instalments,” he said.Having heard both parties at length, the National Commission, on October 6, 2026, directed the parties to place on record a copy of the IDV depreciation table pertaining to motor vehicles issued by IRDA (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India).“We find therefrom that in respect of vehicles having crossed the age of four years but not exceeding five years, there is a depreciation of 50%. The vehicle in question at the time of its seizure was already ten years old. So its value would certainly have fallen even below 50 percent. The Insurer had treated its value at Rs.7,69,500/- which is certainly less than 50% of the amount after applying the depreciation of 50%,” the commission observed.The commission calculated the vehicle's value and revised the compensation of Rs 20 lakh awarded by the state commission to the actual IDV of the vehicle, directing the bank to pay Rs 7.7 lakh with interest.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news. articles.title: In 2024, MacKenzie Scott invited nonprofits to apply for her $640 million philanthropic fund; after receiving 6,000 applications, she selected 361 organisations, giving 279 of them $2 million each
articles.summary: In 2024, billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott opened her philanthropic fund to nonprofits, distributing $640 million to 361 organizations, empowering those addressing systemic inequalities.
articles.body: Billionaire philanthropist MacKenzie Scott expanded her charitable giving in 2024 after an open application process attracted more than 6,000 nonprofit organisations seeking financial support. She ultimately selected 361 groups, with 279 receiving $2 million each and another 82 receiving $1 million each, bringing the total distribution to $640 million.The initiative marked a change in how Scott identified organisations for funding—rather than relying exclusively on private research to find potential recipients, her philanthropic organisation, Yield Giving, invited nonprofits to submit applications directly.The original plan was to distribute $250 million through 250 grants of $1 million each. However, the number of applications and the work highlighted by participating organisations led the team overseeing the programme to increase both the number of recipients and the overall funding.Why MacKenzie Scott opened her philanthropic fund to applicationsScott's 2024 initiative, known as the Yield Giving Open Call, offered nonprofit organisations an opportunity to seek funding directly rather than waiting to be approached by her team.Previously, her organisation had largely followed a different process. It conducted what it described as 'quiet research', identifying groups working in communities and contacting selected organisations privately to offer financial support.The open application model brought a wider range of organisations into the selection process. More than 6,000 groups submitted applications, with 361 eventually chosen across 38 US states.In announcing the recipients, Scott said they had been selected for their work in expanding opportunities for people from low-income backgrounds and communities facing discrimination and systemic barriers.The selected organisations were recognised for their efforts to address inequalities in areas including education, healthcare and economic opportunities.How the $640 million was distributed among 361 organisationsThe final allocation was considerably larger than the amount initially announced for the programme.Of the 361 selected nonprofits, 279 received grants of $2 million each, while the remaining 82 were awarded $1 million apiece. This brought the total funding to $640 million, according to Yield Giving.The organisation said the selected groups were creating positive change in their communities by addressing disparities in economic outcomes, education, health and other important areas.Among the recipients were the ACLU of Alabama, Black Girl Ventures, GLBTQ Legal Advocates and Defenders, Ser Familia, Justice for Migrant Women, the Sacramento LGBT Community Center and Mental Health Advocacy Services.The selection process was managed with support from Lever for Change, which handled the applications and evaluation process. The organisation said the strength of the submissions prompted the decision to increase the number and value of the grants.How much has MacKenzie Scott donated since her divorce from Jeff Bezos?Scott's $640 million distribution was part of a wider philanthropic effort that gathered pace after her 2019 divorce from Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.As part of the settlement, she received a 4% stake in Amazon, which significantly increased her personal wealth. She subsequently signed the Giving Pledge, committing to donate the majority of her fortune to charitable causes during her lifetime.Her donations have supported organisations working across education, public health, the arts and social equality. In 2023, she distributed more than $2 billion to around 360 organisations.According to Forbes, in 2024, Scott was the fourth-richest woman in the world, with an estimated net worth of nearly $35 billion.
